title: Quarterly Commitment Hedge & Operator Handbook for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Isha Patel
description: Objective: produce an operational handbook and quarterly plan that ties Hosted API commitment lanes to concrete hedges, fallthroughs, and model-catalog rotation policies. The deliverable will be a single-page operator runbook + a companion spreadsheet of hedges (capacity, model downgrades, regional fallbacks, promo throttles) and an OKR-aligned scorecard for tracking in the Console. This ticket coordinates PM, infra SRE, and capacity planning to reduce surprise spend during surge scenarios and make canary windows deterministic.
background: We observed two Q1 incidents where demand mismatches and model-swap latencies caused cascading rate-limit enforcement and customer-facing 5xx. Current runbooks cover incident response but not pre-commit hedges or rollout fallthroughs tied to the model catalog. This work addresses the gap by synthesizing policy into a quarterly commitment playbook that product owners and operators can follow.
acceptance_criteria: Operator handbook (1 page) committed to Confluence with step-by-step hedge activation matrix
Hedge spreadsheet with explicit knobs: reserved-GPU-slices, burst-credit thresholds, regional failover order, model downgrade map, and per-customer throttle profiles
Automated alerting thresholds mapped to handbook actions and wired into the Console runbook dashboard
Canary windows and rollback criteria defined for at least 3 model families in the catalog
OKR-linked scorecard template added to the Q2 initiative board and marked as tracker in the PM dashboard
Handbook reviewed and approved by SRE lead and Head of Product (signoffs recorded in updates)
notes: Trade-off: prefer smaller, automated hedges (burst credits + model downgrade) over large reserved capacity buys to keep price competitiveness for self-serve customers
Decision: two-stage hedge model — soft hedges (automated throttles, cache prioritization) vs hard hedges (reserved GPU slices, manual throttles) mapped to SLA tiers
Open question: whether per-route canaries are mature enough to support automated downgrade; added follow-up ENG spike to validate (ENG-40890)
Cost model: finance needs a cost delta estimate for each hedge; paired with Finance owner Ana Ruiz to get baseline numbers by 2026-03-18
